title: Kerala Monsoon Death Toll Climbs to Six as Floods and Landslips Ravage Kottayam
excerpt: Heavy rainfall has triggered landslips and caused rivers to overflow across Kerala's Kottayam district, killing at least six people as the India Meteorological Department warns of continued downpours.
body:
• At least six people killed in rain-related incidents across Kerala's Kottayam district, up from two earlier this week
  • Landslips and overflowing rivers have left a trail of destruction, damaging homes, roads, and bridges in multiple locations
  • IMD has issued orange and red alerts for several Kerala districts including Kottayam, Idukki, and Ernakulam
  • Kerala's 2026 monsoon season has been marked by recurring deadly events, including the Kalladi landslide in Wayanad that killed eight in July

Kottayam Bears the Brunt

The death toll from monsoon-related flooding in Kerala's Kottayam district has climbed to six, authorities confirmed, as relentless heavy rainfall triggered landslips and sent rivers surging past their banks across the southern Indian state.

The casualties, which rose from two deaths reported earlier in the week, include victims of landslides in hilly areas and drownings caused by flash flooding. Rescue teams from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and state fire services have been deployed to affected areas, with operations continuing despite difficult conditions.

Rivers Overflow, Infrastructure Crumbles

Overflowing rivers have inundated low-lying areas across Kottayam, one of Kerala's central districts known for its rubber plantations and proximity to the Western Ghats. Roads have been damaged at multiple points, bridges submerged, and dozens of families evacuated from waterlogged homes to relief camps.

The India Meteorological Department has maintained orange alerts for Kottayam, Idukki, and Ernakulam districts, warning of heavy to very heavy rainfall. Red alerts, signalling the possibility of extremely heavy rain exceeding 20 cm in 24 hours, have been issued for parts of the state's highland districts.

A Monsoon Season of Cascading Disasters

The Kottayam flooding is the latest in a series of monsoon tragedies to strike Kerala in 2026. On July 7, a major landslide at a tunnel construction site in Wayanad's Kalladi killed eight people and injured ten, drawing national attention to infrastructure safety in the ecologically fragile Western Ghats. That disaster prompted renewed scrutiny of construction practices in landslide-prone zones, after investigators found that warnings from the Geological Survey of India had gone unheeded.

Further landslides and flooding incidents have been reported in Idukki district, where at least one more person died on August 1 after a motorcycle was buried under debris. Traffic has been suspended on sections of the Kochi-Dhanushkodi Highway due to landslide damage.

"A 24-hour alert has to be observed and all those living close to water sources have to be very cautious."

— Kerala state advisory

Pattern of Vulnerability

Kerala has experienced devastating monsoon flooding repeatedly in recent years. The 2018 floods killed over 400 people and displaced more than a million, while the 2024 Wayanad landslides claimed over 200 lives. Climate scientists have warned that warming Arabian Sea surface temperatures and altered monsoon circulation patterns are producing more intense, erratic rainfall across the Western Ghats, turning once-predictable monsoons into sequences of extreme weather events.

The state government has urged residents in flood-prone and landslide-vulnerable areas to evacuate to safer locations. Relief camps have been established across affected districts, with supplies being distributed by state and central government agencies.

What's Next

IMD forecasts indicate continued heavy rainfall across Kerala through at least the first week of August, with conditions expected to remain hazardous in highland and coastal areas alike. Authorities have asked fishermen to avoid venturing into the Arabian Sea amid rough sea conditions. The state disaster management authority continues to monitor dam water levels across Kerala's reservoir network, with controlled releases already underway at several facilities to prevent catastrophic overflow.
nri_angle: Keralites abroad, one of India's largest diaspora communities, closely monitor monsoon conditions given family members and property in flood-prone areas.
